A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. Existing appendix material is retained, with Appendix A.9 added in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on truth-vector geometry across four LLMs, including random-context comparisons, probing results and correlation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds steering intervention outcomes in Appendix A.9 and Tables 11–12.

M1.justification: The geometric analysis method in Section 3 is unchanged. Appendix A.9 adds an inference intervention using unit-normalized mass-mean truth vectors and signed steering strengths, a limited procedural extension for validating the representations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight subsets from DRUID, MF2, LegalBench and ConflictQA. The steering experiment reuses the existing truth-label tasks and with-context/without-context conditions; it adds an intervention procedure rather than new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The logistic regression, linear SVM, mass-mean and MLP probe comparisons remain unchanged, as do the five random-context controls. The newly cited Angular Steering work is discussed but is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix A.9 introduces a distinct intervention-based evaluation protocol: derive steering directions from the existing 80% training partition, measure output-label switching on the 20% test partition, and vary layers and strengths to report maximum switching. This substantially extends evaluation beyond geometric measurements and probing without revising the earlier protocols.

E4.justification: v1 explicitly leaves interventional experiments for future work. v2 adds a study testing whether the extracted truth directions can change generated labels across all four models and eight subsets, with and without context. This substantially expands functional validation; the earlier supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Wilcoxon tests, Bonferroni corrections and standard-error plots are retained unchanged. The new steering results do not introduce repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or additional significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 and the existing plotted findings are unchanged. Table 11 adds best-setting label-switching rates, including 100% throughout for SmolLM and 11.43% for Qwen on ConflictQA-Counter with context. Table 12 adds selected layers and strengths. These are new intervention results, not improvements over comparable v1 scores.

T1.justification: The truth-vector, angular-change and relative-magnitude definitions and Equations 1–13 remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central geometric findings and contribution scope remain unchanged. The abstract and conclusion remove explicit 'first work' wording, but Section 1 retains the same priority claim, so the paper does not withdraw or redefine its claimed novelty.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses about competing context and memory signals and dimensionality-related interference, asserts functional relevance from steering, and introduces RAG diagnostics and magnitude-focused steering implications in Section 5.5. Section 7 replaces the deferred-intervention limitation with uncertainty about transfer to reasoning models. These substantially expand interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly states model activation dimensions and documents steering-vector normalization, label-switch verification, selected layers and strengths, and the strength-sign convention. Existing hardware, decoding, computational-cost and code-link disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Vu and Nguyen's Angular Steering (2025) and positions its findings as a possible explanation for interference during steering in smaller models. The existing related-work section and other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 renames Sections 4 and 5, adds Practical Implications, Steering Intervention and Acknowledgements sections, and makes localized paragraph and wording edits. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–12 with separate context-condition panels and rearranges existing tables and appendix figures, including separating Figures 9 and 10 onto different pages. Existing raster plots are downsampled while retaining their plotted content; there is no wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.9 adds useful intervention evidence where v1 explicitly deferred it, and Tables 11–12 document outcomes and selected configurations. This improves functional validation while retaining the original evidence. The gain is limited because the reported maxima lack random-direction controls and uncertainty estimates, and the new dimensionality explanations and RAG applications are not directly tested.
